record.paper_title: Open Problems on Connectivity of Fibers with Positive Margins in Multi-dimensional Contingency Tables
record.context_brief: Positive-marginal connectivity for m-covariate logistic regression
record.original_question: Consider logistic regression with m covariates. For a level combination j = (j_1, ..., j_m), let e_j be the array with 1 at cell (1, j) and −1 at cell (2, j). Define B_{Λ(A_1⊗···⊗A_m)} to be the set of moves m of the form m = e_{j_1} − e_{j_2} − e_{j_3} + e_{j_4} such that j_1 − j_2 = j_3 − j_4. Does this set of moves connect every fiber whose response marginals are all positive for the logistic regression model with m covariates?

evidence.quote: Then we have the following conjecture. Conjecture 2. The set of moves BΛ(A1⊗···⊗Am) connects every fiber with positive response marginals for the logistic regression with m covariates.

Theorem 5 shows the connectivity result for fibers with positive response variable marginals for bivariate logistic regression. There is a natural extension of Theorem 5 to m covariates: Let j = (j1, . . . , jm) denote the combination of m levels and let ej denote an array with 1 at the cell (1, j) and −1 at the cell (2, j). Define BΛ(A1⊗···⊗Am) as the set of the following moves m: 1. m = ej1 − ej2 − ej3 + ej4 2. j1 − j2 = j3 − j4 .

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a logistic regression model with $m$ categorical covariates, where the $k$-th covariate takes $I_k$ levels. The data are organized as a $2 \times I_1 \times \cdots \times I_m$ contingency table $x = (x_{i,j_1,\dots,j_m})$, where $i \in \{1,2\}$ indexes the binary response and $(j_1,\dots,j_m) \in \prod_{k=1}^m \{1,\dots,I_k\}$ indexes a covariate-level combination. The sufficient statistics for the logistic regression model with main effects $1, j_1, \dots, j_m$ on the logit are: (i) the column sums $n_{j_1,\dots,j_m} = x_{1,j_1,\dots,j_m} + x_{2,j_1,\dots,j_m}$ for each $(j_1,\dots,j_m)$, and (ii) the linear statistics $\sum_{j_1,\dots,j_m} j_k\, x_{1,j_1,\dots,j_m}$ for $k=1,\dots,m$. A fiber is the set of nonnegative integer arrays sharing the same sufficient statistics. The fiber is said to have positive response marginals if both $\sum_{j} x_{1,j} > 0$ and $\sum_{j} x_{2,j} > 0$.

For a level combination $j = (j_1,\dots,j_m)$, let $e_j$ be the $2 \times I_1 \times \cdots \times I_m$ integer array with entry $+1$ at cell $(1, j)$, entry $-1$ at cell $(2, j)$, and zeros elsewhere. Define the set of moves
$$
B_{\Lambda(A_1 \otimes \cdots \otimes A_m)} = \{\, e_{j^{(1)}} - e_{j^{(2)}} - e_{j^{(3)}} + e_{j^{(4)}} \;:\; j^{(1)} - j^{(2)} = j^{(3)} - j^{(4)} \in \mathbb{Z}^m \,\},
$$
where each $j^{(\ell)} \in \prod_k \{1,\dots,I_k\}$. Each such move preserves the sufficient statistics above.

Question: Does $B_{\Lambda(A_1 \otimes \cdots \otimes A_m)}$ connect every fiber with positive response marginals? That is, for every two nonnegative integer arrays $x, y$ in the same fiber having positive response marginals, does there exist a sequence $x = z^{(0)}, z^{(1)}, \dots, z^{(N)} = y$ of nonnegative integer arrays in the fiber such that each successive difference $z^{(t)} - z^{(t-1)}$ lies in $B_{\Lambda(A_1 \otimes \cdots \otimes A_m)}$?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not surface a published proof or counterexample to this conjecture for general $m$ covariates. The bivariate ($m=2$) case is established, and the general-$m$ statement is posed as a conjecture; no later work resolving it was located. Status appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On connectivity of fibers with positive marginals in multiple logistic regression
status_evidence.snippet: Connectivity result established for bivariate logistic regression with positive response marginals; extension to m covariates posed.
status_evidence.claim: The bivariate case is solved; the m-covariate generalization is the natural open conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Markov Chains, Quotient Ideals, and Connectivity with Positive Margins
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses positive-margin connectivity questions for logistic regression Markov bases.
status_evidence.claim: Topic remains an active research direction without a complete resolution found.
